description: Figure 5(a) displays training loss curves for various methods during training from scratch, plotting the loss ratio on the y-axis against the number of iterations on the x-axis. The y-axis, labeled "Loss Ratio," ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 and uses a linear scale. The x-axis, labeled "Iteration," spans from 0 to 140,000 and also uses a linear scale, with tick marks appearing at intervals of 20,000. The plot contains five distinct lines, each representing a different method: a purple dashed line for "Vanilla," a blue dashed line for "StrmLLM (n=64)," an orange dashed line for "SepLLM (n=64)," a green dashed line for "SepLLM (n=64, H)," and a red dashed line for "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)." All lines begin at a loss ratio of approximately 3.1 to 3.2 and exhibit a downward trend as iterations increase, converging toward a loss ratio near 2.5. The "Vanilla" line starts at the highest loss ratio and declines the slowest, while the "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" line starts at a lower loss ratio and declines the fastest, reaching below 2.5 by approximately 140,000 iterations.
